inputs.text: [excited][playful] Here we are in the [serious] Ice Age! [happily] Later on, the cold comes back. [serious] Really cold. [gasps] The continents get covered in ice for millions of years.
[playful][happily] A lot! [excited] Ice spreads across Europe and North America. [softly] Animals adapt: thick fur, fat under the skin.
[excited] The woolly mammoth, [quickly] a cousin of the elephant with fur down to its feet! [happily] The saber-tooth cat. Wolves. Cave bears.

[happily][excited] Yes! [gasps] About two and a half million years ago, in Africa, the first humans appear. [playful] They walk upright, and they eat everything: plants, fruit, seeds, meat. [softly] They're hunter-gatherers.
[playful][happily] Not quite! [excited] About three hundred thousand years ago, Homo sapiens arrives. [gasps] That's our direct ancestor: humans just like us today.
[excited][quickly] Humans get really clever. [happily] They light fires, they talk, they make sharp tools. [softly] They hunt big animals and shelter from the cold.
[happily][excited] The kings of the planet! [gasps] The ultimate hunters. [quickly] They raise animals, grow crops, build villages, towns, roads, bridges, boats.
[excited][quickly] Even more! [gasps] They invent electricity, the steam engine, the motor. [happily] The car, the train, the telephone.
[excited][quickly] And they fly! [happily] In hot-air balloons, in planes, in rockets. [softly] Humans learn to master animals, nature, and the forces of physics.
[softly] We're almost caught up to today. [happily] Ready to find out [pauses] how we know all this?
